statement: Quraysh bound themselves by a written pact against Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib: no marriage, no trade, until they surrendered the Prophet; the document was hung inside the Ka'bah.
notes: The existence and terms of the pact are confirmed by Bukhari 1590; the written document and its hanging in the Ka'bah are from the Seerah.

statement: Both clans, believers and non-believers, withdrew to the ravine of Abu Talib; Abu Lahab alone sided with Quraysh.
The boycott began in the seventh year of the mission and lasted two to three years.
alternatives: Most say three years (Muharram year 7 to Muharram year 10); some say two.

statement: Food came only secretly or in the sacred months; merchants outbid them; they ate leaves; children's crying was heard.
Hakim ibn Hizam and Hisham ibn Amr sent food in secretly; the Prophet continued calling people during the sacred months.
Hisham ibn Amr gathered five men, including al-Mut'im ibn Adi, who declared the pact void; it was torn up and the clans came out.
notes: The five: Hisham ibn Amr, Zuhayr ibn Abi Umayyah, al-Mut'im ibn Adi, Abu al-Bakhtari ibn Hisham, Zam'ah ibn al-Aswad.

statement: The Prophet told Abu Talib that termites had eaten the document except the name of Allah, and it was found so.
notes: From Ibn Ishaq and Ibn Sa'd; narrated with attribution. Reviewer to confirm whether to keep.

statement: At Mina during the Farewell Hajj he said they would camp at Khayf Bani Kinanah where the oath of disbelief was sworn: the pact of Quraysh and Kinanah against Banu Hashim and Banu al-Muttalib not to intermarry or trade until they handed over the Prophet.
notes: Machine-checked. The explanation of the place is the narrator's, within the hadith.
